top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is one identifiable invention, magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the differential light shift while many atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime free of Doppler and recoil shifts. Its realization at about 10^-18 has been reproduced in several laboratories and species and checked by clock comparisons. That is a different regime from the 2005 comb and the 2012 single-ion control, and the two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first realization, Ye for record accuracy and the many-body clock) follows the invention. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is exciting and new, but its pairing physics is still moving and three names leave out Yuan Cao and the early confirming groups. It is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No conflict with Katori or Ye apparent from profile; only general atomic-physics proximity and long-standing collaborations with Lund and ETH attosecond groups, which do not concern this proposal.
